title: Partially-Structured Transformer Pruning with Patch-Limited XOR-Gate Compression for Stall-Free Sparse-Model Access
problem: Accessing sparse transformer models suffers from frequent memory stalls due to irregular memory access patterns caused by pruning. This prevents achieving ideal speedup despite significant model compression.
motivation: Efficient deployment of large transformer models in practical services requires eliminating memory stalls to achieve real speedup during inference.
method: The approach limits the number of patches per weight in XOR-gate compression to enforce regular, stall-free memory access patterns. Partially-structured pruning patterns are applied to minimize correction patches and improve accuracy-bandwidth trade-offs. Aggressive per-weight patch distribution adjustment keeps the patch count below weight bits, maximizing effective bandwidth.
key_novelty: Limiting patches per weight to enforce stall-free regular memory access in sparse transformers while maintaining accuracy through partially-structured pruning patterns.
contributions: Novel partially-structured pruning method designed for XOR-gate compression with interface-friendly format
Stall-free memory access mechanism by limiting patches per weight with principled accuracy-bandwidth trade-off
Reduced correction patches through partially-structured patterns for improved efficiency
Highest effective bandwidth for sparse transformer inference on DeiT/BERT compared to existing solutions

metrics.speedup: highest effective bandwidth for sparse transformer access
metrics.accuracy: maintains model accuracy with patch-bandwidth optimization

limitations: Evaluation limited to DeiT and BERT models; broader applicability to other transformer architectures and training scenarios not discussed.
primary_theme: stall-free sparse transformer inference via structured pruning
